subject: Risk & Compliance
title: Wells Fargo's Toxic Incentives
description: A fast breakdown of Wells Fargo's Toxic Incentives for builders.

hook.text: Wells Fargo employees created 3.5 million fake accounts to meet sales targets. Management called it 'cross-selling.'

buildup.text: The bank's 'Eight is Great' campaign pushed employees to open eight products per customer, regardless of need.

discovery.text: Employees who refused to create fake accounts were fired. Those who called ethics hotlines faced retaliation.

twist.text: CEO John Stumpf initially blamed 5,300 low-level employees. He was eventually forced to resign and return $41 million.

climax.text: Toxic incentives created the fraud. A culture of fear sustained it. The failure was systemic, not individual.

punchline.text: 3.5 million fake accounts. Blame the tellers. Culture did this.

quiz.question: What drove Wells Fargo employees to create fake accounts?
options: Aggressive sales targets and fear of being fired
